newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end sharply lower, led by gold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end sharply lower, led by gold.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended sharply lower Tuesday, led by heavy fund selling in COMEX gold futures on a break of month-old chart support levels with encouragement from lower-than-expected U.S. March consumer prices.

"It's a no-win situation for gold," Merrill Lynch commodities research director Bill O'Neill said. "Rising real interest rates undermined the attraction of gold in the past few weeks, but when interest rates fell today in response to the inflation data, gold fell still further as low inflation also means gold is less attractive."

"Volumes have been low on the recent slide, but we saw the heaviest volume for some weeks today and it looks like gold is going down to test the three year lows around $336.00 seen in spot gold in February," he said.
COMEX June gold ended down $4.80 at $344.10 an ounce after some late shortcovering by day traders lifted the contract off its session low of $342.30.
Estimated total COMEX gold volume was a high 60,000 lots, but open interest as of Monday was still near its lowest levels for a year at 150,382 contracts.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted at $341.70/$342.20 compared to the London afternoon fix of $343.00 and the New York close Monday of $346.50/$347.00.

After between $348 and $358 in the past month, the latest slide was led by Australian producer selling overnight, combined with the execution of stop orders by funds below $348.00 in the June contract, traders said.
But a less-than-expected U.S. March CPI rise of only 0.1 percent also added to reasons for disinvestment from gold, analysts said.
Gold was weaker than silver Tuesday, with the spot gold/silver ratio slipping back to 72.3 from 73.3 Monday, after recovering to a three-month high of 73.5 April 4.
COMEX May silver ended down 1.5 cents at $4.71 after recovering from an early low of $4.66, not far from the contract low at $4.655 posted April 3.
Spot silver was quoted $4.72/4.74, after a dip toward the three-month low of $4.65 set in early January.
Gold was also weaker than platinum Tuesday, with the October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread edging up above $20.00 intraday before closing little changed around $19.30.
NYMEX July platinum ended down $2.70 at $367.50 after testing the early-April lows around $365 during the session.

In news Tuesday, South Africa's Anglo American Platinum Corp (Amplats) said it expected the world platinum surplus to fall to 65,000 ounces in 1997, from 80,000 in 1996, and predicted growing demand for the metal into the next century.
Amplats expects 1997 supply to total 4.963 million ounces, against demand of 4.898 million, compared to supply of 4.850 million ounces in 1996 and demand of 4.770 million.
The company also announced a major expansion of its operations with a new platinum mine at Boschkoppie in the Rustenberg area of South Africa and an expansion of Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd.
NYMEX June palladium lost $3.85 to $150.10, with traders expecting talks on a resumption of Russian PGM supplies to Japan this month.
The world's largest palladium producer, Russia, has been out of the market for most of this year, resulting in a rundown of world inventories.
Short-term palladium lease rates were reported to have slipped back under 10 percent Tuesday, as tightness in the prompt market eased.
Lease rates jumped to around 16-20 percent last week as trade houses in Switzerland and Japan were forced to borrow metal to meet forward sales deliveries.
